hints.text: Look at the input coins=[3,8] and amount=28. In your loop, you first use coin 8 repeatedly. Which line of your code handles this?

Your algorithm uses all 8-cent coins first, leaving a remainder of 4. Since 4 cannot be made with 3-cent coins, the algorithm returns -1, but a solution exists using four 3-cent coins and two 8-cent coins. This contradicts the assumption that taking the largest coin first always leads to an optimal solution.
What property must a greedy choice satisfy to guarantee optimality in problems like coin change?
